findings.text: Assigns ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_PIC at zero then ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_IOAPIC at one then ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_IOSAPIC at two then ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_PLATFORM at three then ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_GIC at four then ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_GIC_V5 at five then ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_LPIC at six then ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_RINTC at seven then ACPI_IRQ_MODEL_COUNT at eight.

Assigns ACPI_INTERRUPT_PMI at one then ACPI_INTERRUPT_INIT at two then ACPI_INTERRUPT_CPEI at three then ACPI_INTERRUPT_COUNT at four and sets ACPI_SPACE_MEM at zero and assigns ACPI_ADDRESS_RANGE_MEMORY at one then ACPI_ADDRESS_RANGE_RESERVED at two then ACPI_ADDRESS_RANGE_ACPI at three then ACPI_ADDRESS_RANGE_NVS at four then ACPI_ADDRESS_RANGE_COUNT at five.
Defines the acpi_tbl_table_handler callback contract where the callee receives a table header and returns an integer status for the handling attempt.

Orders acpi_debugger_ops with create_thread then write_log then read_cmd then wait_command_ready then notify_command_complete where creation accepts an execution callback plus context and logging accepts a message and reading accepts a buffer plus length and waiting accepts stepping mode plus buffer plus length and completion accepts no input and orders acpi_debugger with ops then owner then lock where ops refers to the operations and owner refers to the module and lock serializes access.
Requires that access to the debugger instance be serialized through its embedded mutex with ownership and lifetime coordinated alongside the operations reference and module owner.

In the configuration without debugger support acpi_debugger_init plus acpi_register_debugger plus acpi_debugger_create_thread plus acpi_debugger_write_log plus acpi_debugger_read_cmd plus acpi_debugger_wait_command_ready plus acpi_debugger_notify_command_complete each report negative ENODEV while acpi_unregister_debugger performs no action.

Treats a MADT subtable entry as invalid when its pointer is missing or its storage would extend past the table bound or its declared length is smaller than its own header, preventing out of bounds interpretation.

Offers a lookup helper that resolves a firmware table by signature and instance, delivering the header on success and an encoded absence error otherwise for the caller to detect without dereferencing.

Encodes negative error numbers as pointer values so that table lookup and subsystem identifier retrieval can signal absence through the return channel, requiring callers to test for encoded errors before use to avoid dereferencing invalid addresses.
Provides empty affinity and DMA setup operations for processor and GICC and RINTC affinity plus device DMA in configurations without the corresponding support, performing no action on their inputs.
Defines phys_cpuid_t as a 32 bit unsigned physical identifier and reserves all bits set as PHYS_CPUID_INVALID to mark the absence of a valid physical identifier.

Considers a logical identifier invalid when its signed interpretation is negative and considers a physical identifier invalid exactly when it matches the reserved invalid sentinel, providing complementary validity tests for the two identifier domains.
In configurations without processor power support control claiming reports false and C state evaluation plus LPI extraction each report negative ENODEV without touching their output structures.
Reserves the maximum unsigned value as INVALID_ACPI_IRQ and treats the system control interrupt as valid exactly when the stored interrupt differs from that reservation.
Defines dispatch callback contracts that translate a global system interrupt number into a firmware node handle for domain lookup and into a firmware handle for direct handle lookup respectively.

In configurations without override support interrupt override lookup reports negative one without producing trigger or polarity outputs and control interrupt penalization performs no action on its inputs.
Defines the wmi_notify_handler callback contract where the callee receives a data object plus a context pointer and returns no result for event delivery.

Assigns ACPI_VIDEO_OUTPUT_SWITCHING at bit zero then ACPI_VIDEO_DEVICE_POSTING at bit one then ACPI_VIDEO_ROM_AVAILABLE at bit two then ACPI_VIDEO_BACKLIGHT at bit three then ACPI_VIDEO_BACKLIGHT_FORCE_VENDOR at bit four then ACPI_VIDEO_BACKLIGHT_FORCE_VIDEO at bit five then ACPI_VIDEO_OUTPUT_SWITCHING_FORCE_VENDOR at bit six then ACPI_VIDEO_OUTPUT_SWITCHING_FORCE_VIDEO at bit seven then ACPI_VIDEO_BACKLIGHT_DMI_VENDOR at bit eight then ACPI_VIDEO_BACKLIGHT_DMI_VIDEO at bit nine then ACPI_VIDEO_OUTPUT_SWITCHING_DMI_VENDOR at bit ten then ACPI_VIDEO_OUTPUT_SWITCHING_DMI_VIDEO at bit eleven.
Reports negative EOPNOTSUPP without producing coordinate output when generic port coordinate retrieval is unavailable for the given identifier.
Translates a proximity domain through node mapping and then through online node selection to yield an online NUMA node for the caller in NUMA capable configurations.

In configurations without NUMA support proximity to online node translation plus proximity to node mapping plus handle to node lookup each report zero as the sole node without inspecting their inputs.
Reserves negative one as PXM_INVAL to mark the absence of a valid proximity domain identifier.
Offers a resource filtering callback that interprets its opaque argument as an encoded resource type and delegates to type based filtering for the given resource.

Orders acpi_osc_context with uuid_str then rev then cap then ret where the first holds a textual UUID and the second holds a revision number and the third carries input capability words and the fourth carries output words owned by the caller after success.
Sets OSC_PCI_CAPABILITY_DWORDS at three words and OSC_CXL_CAPABILITY_DWORDS at five words to size the capability buffers for the respective negotiation types.

Positions OSC_QUERY_DWORD at index zero then OSC_SUPPORT_DWORD at index one then OSC_CONTROL_DWORD at index two then OSC_EXT_SUPPORT_DWORD at index three then OSC_EXT_CONTROL_DWORD at index four for sequential access to negotiation words.

Provides accessors that fetch the PCI control word and the extended CXL control word from the negotiation return storage for the caller.
Assumes the negotiation return storage holds sufficient words for the requested control index, so short or missing buffers would cause out of bounds access during control retrieval.
Declares ACPI_HOTPLUG_OST as a presence marker enabling hotplug status reporting support without carrying a numeric value.
Assigns ACPI_OST_EC_OSPM_SHUTDOWN at 256 then ACPI_OST_EC_OSPM_EJECT at 259 then ACPI_OST_EC_OSPM_INSERTION at 512 for operating system power management event codes.

In enabled configurations ACPI_PTR preserves its input unchanged while device enumeration marking sets the visited flag and clearing resets it, tracking whether a device has been seen.
Distinguishes reconfiguration notifications as device addition at zero versus device removal at one, providing the two event phases for dynamic ACPI topology changes.
Provides architecture root pointer operations that discard the supplied address on setting and report zero on retrieval in configurations without arch specific storage.
Lists CMOS real time clock identifiers as PNP0B00 then PNP0B01 then PNP0B02 closed by an empty terminator for hardware matching.

In disabled configurations platform creation plus resource consumer lookup plus bus name lookup yield null and DMA support reports false with DMA attribute as not supported while DMA range plus local address report negative ENODEV and both DMA configuration variants report zero and pointer macro yields null and both enumeration marking variants perform no action and both reconfiguration registration variants report negative EINVAL and subsystem identifier yields an encoded ENODEV error and wakeup registration reports negative ENXIO with unregistration performing no action.

Exposes firmware table handling through a callback for table notifications plus a direct lookup by signature and instance plus a parser that applies a handler to a named table, forming the table access entry points.
